# MCPcat

> > MCPcat provides observability, testing, and debugging tools for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers used with Claude Code and AI coding assistants.

MCPcat helps developers monitor, test, and secure MCP servers built with Python, Node.js, and TypeScript. The platform offers SDK integration, distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, and comprehensive guides for debugging JSON-RPC errors, security testing, and deployment strategies using stdio and StreamableHTTP transports.

## Key Topics

- Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Claude Code
- MCP servers
- Observability and monitoring
- JSON-RPC protocol
- stdio and StreamableHTTP transports
- Security testing and tool poisoning
- Unit and integration testing
- OpenTelemetry tracing
- Docker deployment
- pytest and testing frameworks
- Connection management
- Error debugging (-32000, -32601)
- Tool input validation
- Claude Desktop integration

## Testing and Validation

- [Unit Testing MCP Servers - Complete Testing Guide | MCPcat](https://mcpcat.io/guides/writing-unit-tests-mcp-servers): Write unit tests for MCP servers using FastMCP, pytest, and in-memory patterns
- [MCP Integration Testing - E2E Testing Guide | MCPcat](https://mcpcat.io/guides/integration-tests-mcp-flows): Write E2E integration tests for MCP workflows with Inspector CLI and pytest
- [MCP Tool Input Validation Testing - Complete Guide | MCPcat](https://mcpcat.io/guides/validation-tests-tool-inputs): Write validation tests for MCP tools using Zod and Pydantic schemas
- [MCP Server Security Testing - Comprehensive Guide | MCPcat](https://mcpcat.io/guides/security-tests-mcp-server-endpoints): Test MCP server security: authentication, authorization, vulnerability scanning
